diagnosis_explanation: You have migraines with aura. This means you get a headache. You might also see flashing lights or colors before your head hurts. It can make it hard to see or feel strange. We do not know what causes these. Many people get them. We have given you medicine to help.
medication_rationale:
Vicodin 5/500 as needed:
This medicine is a pain reliever. It can help with migraine pain. You may feel sleepy or dizzy. This is normal. Call your doctor if you feel very confused. Also call if you have trouble breathing.

Celexa 40 mg daily:
This medicine is for your mood. It can help prevent migraines. You may feel restless or have an upset stomach. This is often mild. Call your doctor if you feel very anxious. Also call if you think about harming yourself.

Phenergan 25 mg as needed:
This medicine can help with nausea or vomiting. It can also make you feel sleepy. You might feel drowsy or have blurry vision. This is common. Call your doctor if you feel very dizzy. Also call if you get a rash.

Abilify 10 mg daily:
This medicine can help prevent migraines. It may also help with mood. You might feel restless or have trouble sleeping. This can improve over time. Call your doctor if you get uncontrolled movements. Also call if you have severe dizziness.

Klonopin 0.5 mg twice daily:
This medicine helps calm your brain. It can help with migraines. You may feel tired or dizzy. This is common. Call your doctor if you have trouble breathing. Also call if you feel very confused.

Tramadol 30 mg as needed:
This medicine is a pain reliever. It can help with migraine pain. You may feel dizzy or sleepy. This is normal. Call your doctor if you have seizures. Also call if you have trouble breathing.

Ranitidine 150 mg twice daily:
This medicine reduces stomach acid. It can help with stomach upset from other medicines. You may get headaches or feel constipated. This is often mild. Call your doctor if you have stomach pain. Also call if you notice blood in your stool.
recovery_trajectory:
**Week 1:**
- You may feel tired and have a headache. This is normal.
- Rest as much as you can.
- You can do light tasks at home if you feel up to it.
- Call your doctor if your headache gets much worse.
- Your goal this week is to rest and drink plenty of fluids.

**Week 2:**
- You might start to feel a bit more energy this week.
- You can try doing light chores if you feel ready.
- Avoid sudden movements or loud noises that could trigger a headache.
- Your goal this week is to walk around your home for a few minutes each day.
- Call your doctor if you have a fever or stiff neck.

**Week 3:**
- You should feel more comfortable and have more energy.
- You can slowly increase your activity level.
- Try to get back to a regular sleep schedule.
- Your goal this week is to walk outside for 10 minutes.
- Call your doctor if your headaches are more frequent or severe.

**Week 4:**
- You should feel much like you did before your migraine.
- You can return to most normal daily activities.
- Continue to avoid things that you know trigger your migraines.
- Your goal this week is to maintain your regular routine.
- Call your doctor if you develop new symptoms like vision changes or numbness.

**When to expect improvement:**
- Most people feel back to normal within 4 to 6 weeks.
- Keep a log of your headaches to share with your doctor.
- Manage stress to help prevent future migraines.
- Follow up with your doctor as recommended.
escalation_guide:
CALL 911 IMMEDIATELY
These symptoms are life-threatening. Do not drive yourself.
- Unresponsive or very sleepy: Your brain is not working right.
- Sudden severe headache: This can be a serious brain bleed.
- Weakness or numbness on one side: These are stroke signs. Minutes matter.
- Trouble breathing or not breathing: Your body needs air now.
- Seizure that will not stop: Call for help right away.
- Chest pain or pressure: Call for help right away.
- Bleeding that will not stop: You may need help now.

GO TO THE ER TODAY
Do not wait until tomorrow. Go within a few hours.
- Fever over 101 degrees: You may have an infection.
- Severe pain medicine does not help: Your pain is too bad.
- Vision loss or changes: This can affect your sight.
- Can not keep fluids down: You are getting too dry.
- Confusion or disorientation: Your mind is not clear.
- New trouble speaking clearly: You may have a stroke.
- Significant weakness or numbness: This can be serious.

CALL YOUR DOCTOR
Call during office hours. Do not go to the ER for these.
- Headache that is slowly getting better: This is a good sign.
- Questions about your medicine: Your doctor can help you.
- Feeling dizzy or lightheaded: This may pass on its own.
- Mild nausea or upset stomach: This can happen with pain.
- Feeling tired or weak: Your iron may still be low.
